item.title: The CounterSide Reboot Has a Name: COUNTERSIDE: A [ANTEXILIAN]
item.description:
The reboot Studio BSide promised when CounterSide shut down has a name: COUNTERSIDE: A [ANTEXILIAN]. The studio opened an official account for the project on September 2, 2026, a week after the original game switched off its servers on August 26 following six years of service.
The account describes the game in four words — a “hardboiled urban lane battler” — which is the clearest signal so far that the CounterSide reboot keeps the real-time lane combat the original was built on, rather than starting from a different genre.
Very little, and the studio has not pretended otherwise. The channel has published three posts: the announcement art with the new logo, a follow-up teaser, and the account itself. There is no platform list, no gameplay footage and no release window. Studio BSide says both will be announced through the project’s own channels.
The announcement illustration puts faces from the original in front of a capital ship, which is as close as the studio has come to saying how much of the old game carries over. The second post, from September 9, is a single line in Korean, Japanese and English: “Do you remember? The day all of our administration failed.”
CounterSide ran for six years before closing on August 26, and the studio committed to a reboot in the same announcement that confirmed the shutdown. Its other live title is Star Savior, the 3D RPG it launched globally in March 2026, so the CounterSide reboot will be the studio’s second live game rather than its only one.
Platforms and a release window are the two details still missing, and Studio BSide has not said when either will arrive.

item.title: Genshin Impact 7.1 Launches September 23 With Vesna, Vodyanitsa and a Free 5-Star
item.description:
The update also carries the game’s sixth anniversary, and with it the most generous giveaway HoYoverse has attached to one: finishing the new Archon Quest lets every player pick a free event-exclusive 5-star character from a set lineup, on top of a free standard 5-star, 1,600 Primogems and 10 Intertwined Fate. The studio laid out the version in its own announcement.
The Archon Quest takes the crisis in Snezhnaya to its head. Players finally meet the Tsaritsa face to face and learn what she has actually been doing with the Gnoses she spent years collecting. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, has been using her authority to hold Snezhnaya back, and the arrival of Rhinedottir, the Ruler of Life, muddies things further.
The quest ends on the front line, fighting alongside Snezhnaya against Ronova, who also becomes a new Weekly Boss. Completing it pays out 620 Primogems. From 7.1 onwards there are also assignments handed out by the Tsaritsa’s Confidential Secretary, which exist to show how she actually governs.
Vesna is a 5-star Anemo Sword user and the youngest Commander in Druzhna history. She converts Cryo Swirl reactions into Stellar Swirl, summons Spirit Blades through her Elemental Skill and banks “Sword Essence” that a special Skill spends to send those blades at enemies; near a Stellar Vortex, their hits count as Stellar Swirl damage. Her Burst calls another wave of blades for AoE Anemo damage and gives Sword Essence back. As a Vila, she can fly while exploring.
Vodyanitsa is a 5-star Hydro Catalyst user, Prima Donna of Snezhnograd’s Korolevskiy Troupe and a Water Imp. Her Elemental Skill turns her into her Water Imp form and holds a song that heals the active character, cuts enemy Hydro and Cryo resistance and raises the active character’s ATK, while the same song strengthens Stellar Vortices by lowering Anemo resistance and pushing Stellar Swirl damage up. Her Burst deals AoE Hydro damage, and out in the world she can stay in Water Imp form even out of the water.
Both headline the first phase of the version’s Event Wishes. Skirk and Escoffier return in the second phase.
Yilong Wharf has been dressed up for the Moonchase Festival, and underneath the celebration sits a mystery from the past that neither Zhongli nor Zibai has cracked. The festival brings three new mini-games built around Liyue thaumaturges and a new 4-star Sword among the rewards.
Elsewhere there is a seasonal snowball event with Snezhnayan children and a tournament prediction event in Natlan covering 16 teams across several days of matches. Miliastra Wonderland gets an autumn lobby built on osmanthus and moon motifs, a free cosmetic set tied to its event, an exclusive headpiece, and an editor expanded with client-side scripting and collaborative editing.
HoYoverse published the Genshin Impact 7.1 trailer on the game’s official channel:

item.title: Aniimo Launches on PS5, Xbox and PC, With Mobile Arriving September 23
item.description:
The studio set the Aniimo launch date in a trailer shown during gamescom Opening Night Live, and the official site now links straight to the live storefronts. Pawprint Studio is the publishing label FunPlus created for the game, and Aniimo is its first release.
Players take the role of Pathfinders on the continent of Idyll, where they seek, capture, battle, research and evolve the magical creatures that live there. More than 200 Aniimo are available at release, and which ones appear depends on systems such as the weather and the biome you are standing in.
The mechanic the game is built around is Twining: instead of only ordering a creature into battle, a Pathfinder merges with it. Twining changes your combat skills and how you move — flying, burrowing, sprinting — and it lets you talk to creatures of the same species, which is how several puzzles open up.
Idyll is split into areas with their own ecosystems and their own creature behaviour, among them Driftwise Meadow and its emotion-based ecology, the fiery Sandcastle Hill and the flowering Rosetower Wood. Away from exploration, the Homeland system lets players farm and harvest alongside their Aniimo, decorate the house, and run facilities powered by the creatures themselves from an RV Campsite.
There is competitive and cooperative play too. The PvP mode Egg Heist puts teams against each other, while co-op runs on three open-world tools: the Horn to call for help from friends or strangers, the Flute to invite others to a spot or find nearby players, and Come to Me to pull allies to you instantly.
The Aniimo launch is accompanied by an official trailer on the game’s channel:
The game is free to download on every platform. PC players can get it on Steam or the Epic Games Store, and console players on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Those two consoles also sell two paid bundles alongside the free client, the Aniimo Pre-Order Pack: Advanced Edition and the Collector’s Edition, which add in-game rewards including a platform-exclusive Fluffy Friend accessory and a battle pass.
Mobile players have one more week to wait: the App Store and Google Play versions go live on September 23. Every store link and the PC requirements are gathered in our Aniimo hub.

item.title: Guardian Tales Farming Spin-Off Codename: Kanon Opens Pre-Registration
item.description:
Guardian Tales is getting a farming spin-off under the working title Codename: Kanon (代号：坎农). Chinese pre-registration is open for the licensed project, which trades the Little Princess and Knight’s usual adventures for crops, animals and life on a pixel-art farm.
The official Bilibili website introduces Kanon as a casual game licensed from Guardian Tales. Its first promotional video was published by the game’s official account on September 4, 2026.
The official first trailer is also available on Bilibili.
According to the official game listing, players can clear land, plant crops and raise animals alongside the Little Princess and Knight. More Canterbury companions arrive as the farm develops, and players can invite them to settle in.
The listed social features include visiting friends’ farms and forming a guild. Progress expands the farm and unlocks further content, with the familiar Guardian Tales cast appearing in a quieter setting.
In a message on the listing, the project team identifies itself as the team responsible for the Chinese version of Guardian Tales. It says the concept was discussed with rights holder KONG, which approved and supported it.
The project is being prepared by that Chinese operations team together with a domestic development team. The message explicitly states that KONG is not handling the game’s development and that the project does not change KONG’s own Guardian Tales development and update plans.
The team plans to launch Kanon first as a mini-program, with an app version to follow. The official listing names Android and iOS, but no release date has been announced.
The developers describe it as a place to spend time with the Little Princess, rather than a replacement for Guardian Tales. Pre-registration currently concerns the Chinese project; an English release or wider global rollout has not been confirmed.

item.title: Pearl in Blue Reveals New Trailer Ahead of TGS 2026
item.description:
Pearl in Blue, the upcoming mobile RPG from Netmarble N2, has a new concept trailer ahead of Tokyo Game Show 2026. Netmarble released the world-focused video on September 11 and confirmed a presentation for September 17 at 14:30 JST.
The publisher’s announcement also confirms that the game will be playable at its TGS booth. Visitors will be able to try a demo and attend stage programming featuring members of the cast and development team.
Netmarble presents Pearl in Blue as a romantic-comedy RPG. Its setting centers on Pearls, manifestations of people’s wishes, and girls whose Pearls have yet to bloom. Players become a manager who supports them as they grow.
The new concept video expands on that setting with previously unseen scenes and a focus on the characters’ emotions and conflicts. It is a world introduction ahead of the exhibition, rather than a release-date announcement.
The Pearl in Blue booth will be in Hall 2, booth 02-N12, at Makuhari Messe. Alongside the playable demo, the publisher has announced a September 17 presentation beginning at 14:30 Japan time.
The stage lineup brings together voice cast members and the development team to introduce the game. Netmarble is also preparing booth activities and promotional merchandise for visitors.
For players following from outside Japan, the released concept trailer is already available through the official Pearl in Blue channel. The upcoming presentation is the next announced opportunity for more information about the project.

item.title: Uta Macross Offline Revival Passes Crowdfunding Goal
item.description:
Uta Macross has passed the ¥30 million crowdfunding goal for its offline revival. The campaign opened on September 10, 2026, and a September 11 update confirmed that support had already exceeded twice the original target.
The official CAMPFIRE project is funding a standalone version of the Macross rhythm game, with AUGUST publishing and xeen developing. The planned release is spring 2027 for PC via Steam, iOS and Android in Japan.
The original Uta Macross: Smartphone De Culture ended service on June 28, 2022. The revival has approval from Macross rights holder BIGWEST and the original publisher, DeNA, and rebuilds the game for offline play.
Its purchase model removes paid gacha and stamina consumption. The planned standard package includes 50 songs, more than 1,000 plates centered on four-star rarity and above, and over 20 outfits per character available from the start.
Plate upgrades will still use a random draw system, but the draws use items earned through play and carry no real-money charge. The team plans to change this to a box-style system to make completing the available pool easier.
Additional paid DLC packs are planned alongside the base game, adding songs, plates and outfits that are not included in the standard package. The base package is required to use them; purchasing it does not automatically include every item from the former live service.
Crowdfunding runs until October 31 at 23:59 JST. The project uses an all-in model and says development will go ahead regardless of whether the initial funding goal is met. Following the rapid start, the organizers have added stretch goals.
The campaign includes information for international supporters, but the announced game release is currently Japan-only. Game keys offered as rewards are Steam keys for the Japanese store, rather than mobile downloads. Broader language and platform support is an expansion objective, not a confirmed global launch.

item.title: Made in Abyss Mobile Game Delayed Beyond September 2026
item.description:
Made in Abyss: An Irredeemable Journey of Mysteries has been delayed beyond the September 2026 date shown on app stores. The team announced the change on September 10, saying it needs more time to polish the mobile game. A replacement release date has not been confirmed.
The announcement specifically warns that release dates still displayed by app stores do not reflect the actual launch date. Players waiting for the game should therefore treat the schedule as unconfirmed until the team issues another announcement.
The statement provides neither a new month nor a separate regional timetable. It also does not set out a revised list of features or explain individual development problems; the confirmed change is the postponement of the release.
Published by Avex Pictures and developed by Nobollel, the game adapts the Made in Abyss anime into a mobile roguelike. Its earlier English reveal described it as a deck-building game and opened pre-registration.
The official Google Play listing outlines four parts of the adventure: collecting and upgrading character cards, equipping relics found in the Abyss, choosing routes while managing supplies, and fighting the creatures waiting deeper below.
Those systems tie preparation to exploration: cards strengthen the Cave Raider, relics provide additional powers, and route choices alter the course of a run. The game is being prepared for iOS and Android. Further scheduling news will be shared through its official account.

item.title: SAKAMOTO DAYS Mission: Rogue Dawn Launches in Japan
item.description:
SAKAMOTO DAYS Mission: Rogue Dawn launched in Japan on September 11, 2026, bringing Rudel’s character-training and roguelite action game to iOS and Android. The mobile adaptation of the anime is free to download, with optional in-app purchases.
Rudel’s launch announcement introduces a game built around developing characters and then putting those builds into combat. Players can download it through the Japanese App Store or Google Play; the announcement concerns the Japanese release.
Rogue Dawn combines its action stages with character development. Training lets players acquire skills and shape a character’s stats, with support cards and items contributing to the build. That leaves room to focus on particular strengths or work toward a more balanced character.
The official website describes movement-based controls with automatic attacks, designed for one-handed play. Skills change the options available during a run, while support characters can join the fight. The launch materials show familiar faces including Taro Sakamoto and Shin Asakura.
Trained characters can then take on more demanding content. The site’s Challengers Stage pits those builds against harder stages and includes rankings based on how far players progress. Returning to training provides a way to prepare a different or stronger build for another attempt.
The short gameplay video hosted on the official site offers a look at the action:
Watch the official gameplay video.
Rogue Dawn is a separate title from SAKAMOTO DAYS Dangerous Puzzle. Players looking for the new release should check the full Mission: Rogue Dawn subtitle on the store listing. Rudel has not announced a global launch date in this release.

item.title: Azur Promilia Sets September 17 for Its China Wayfare Test
item.description:
Azur Promilia will begin its Wayfare Test in China on September 17, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. UTC+8. The official announcement sets pre-downloads for September 15 and confirms a limited test on Windows PC, Android and iOS.
The Azur Promilia September beta includes payments and will wipe its game data when it ends. Access requires selection; downloading the client does not make this an open beta.
Test access cannot be sold, rented, shared or given away. The team also requires real-name verification and excludes minors from participating. This remains a development build, with progress scheduled to be erased after testing.
The official recruitment instructions say selected participants must use the TapTap ID and phone number entered in their application. The team recommends the TapTap PC launcher for the Windows version. Qualification messages are delivered through TapTap’s inbox.
The Azur Promilia September beta is a new test following the earlier Constant Order CBT2. Its September opening is a China test date, not a global launch date.
Manjuu’s fantasy RPG pairs its characters with creatures called Kibo. The official English website introduces the cast and some of those companions, while the September test notices cover access to the Chinese build.

item.title: Medabots S Opens Global Pre-Registration After Six Years in Japan
item.description:
Medabots S has opened global pre-registration on iOS and Android, more than six years after its Japanese debut. Imagineer’s official announcement on September 4 links to both mobile stores and previews the robot RPG in a new promotional video.
Medabots S global pre-registration is available through the App Store and Google Play. The announcement does not set a release date, and the official account notes that store availability may be delayed.
Watch the official Medabots S pre-registration video
Build a robot squad for 3v3 Robattles The English store description centres on 3v3 command-based battles, known as Robattles. Players assemble robots from a head, right arm, left arm and legs, then fit a Medal that acts as the machine’s brain.
Those parts are also central to combat: players issue commands for individual components and can upgrade the equipment they want to keep using. Destroying the enemy leader’s head wins the battle, making the choice of target part of the strategy.
The listing also promises an original story and returning characters from across the series. It does not specify a complete global launch roster or a schedule for bringing over Japanese collaborations.
The Japanese game launched on January 23, 2020, as confirmed by Imagineer’s original release notice. That notice credits SoWhat as developer and Imagineer as publisher of the Japanese version.
For players who have followed the series outside Japan, Medabots S global pre-registration is the next step toward an English mobile release. Launch timing and the opening content lineup remain details to watch for in Imagineer’s announcements.
